title: Linearity of the discrete derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $c,d\in\mathbb R$. The discrete derivative in direction $i$ of the function $x\mapsto c f(x)+d g(x)$ is the function $x\mapsto c(D_i f)(x)+d(D_i g)(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f,g$ are real-valued functions on the $n$-dimensional Boolean hypercube
replaced: For any real functions $f,g$ on $\{0,1\}^n$, real scalars $c,d$, and a coordinate $i<n$, $D_i(cf+dg)=cD_i f+dD_i g$, where $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$.
